Does neural internal noise help sparse-view force reconstruction?

36 fixed fits: four synthetic conditions, three seeds and three noise models. Every model receives the same six moving-camera images, force prior and initialization. Both constant and neural balanced internal diffusion are compared with the current full-rank floor. All use exact conditional Gaussian force elimination. Read accuracy, uncertainty width, CRPS and inference flags together.

Mean gap errors on stochastic condition/seed cases: Current floor 4.847 mm, Constant internal 2.893 mm, Neural internal 2.974 mm. On deterministic cases: Current floor 2.819 mm, Constant internal 2.609 mm, Neural internal 2.623 mm. These are averages of per-seed coordinate RMSEs, with three underlying seeds and matched noise across conditions; the paired cases are not six independent realizations. Small differences between neural and constant diffusion do not establish a neural-specific benefit.

What the experiment tests

The current model has independent free-node velocity discrepancy. The constant and neural models add equal/opposite central internal impulses with the same rank-three spatial basis. Neural amplitudes depend on inferred strain and preceding-velocity speed; the constant amplitude matches RMS neural output on separate calibration features. Constant amplitude still follows changing edge directions, so its covariance depends on deformed geometry. The 33-parameter neural network is frozen after independent synthetic training, not learned from the sparse test video. All retain the same fixed discrepancy floor.

This is a noise-model comparison with force marginalization held fixed. It does not independently measure marginalization versus joint fitting; that was a separate v0.6 comparison. Adding internal diffusion may help stochastic motion but can introduce unnecessary flexibility on deterministic motion. Three seeds are exploratory.

Uncertainty and force attribution

Local Gaussian intervals use a metric accounting for both residual-mean and covariance derivatives; this is not the exact posterior Hessian or established calibration. Coverage counts correlated free-node components. CRPS rewards accuracy and appropriate width together. 36/36 fits pass stationarity and 16/36 pass the independent 128-proposal weight-concentration screen; individual flags follow below. Passing is not proof of adequate posterior exploration.

What marginalization contributes

For an inferred path z, mechanical residual r(z)=G a+eta has Gaussian force coefficients a and state-dependent disturbance covariance Q(z). Integrating a gives C(z)=Q(z)+G G^T. The exact conditional force covariance is S(z)=[I+G^T Q(z)^(-1)G]^(-1). Both log determinants and derivatives of Q are retained.

This removes the separate force-update loop and preserves the full conditional force distribution. The trajectory/material problem still requires nonlinear optimization. With fixed Q/G, marginal and best-force joint trajectory optima coincide; no universal speed/accuracy gain follows. With state-dependent Q, marginal_NLL=min_force joint_NLL+0.5 logdet[I+G^T Q^(-1)G]+constant. That varying force-volume correction distinguishes marginalization from choosing only the best force.

Force covariance is E[S(z)]+Cov[m(z)] over local trajectory draws; unlike v0.6, the first term varies and is averaged. Exact force elimination does not make the remaining trajectory posterior exact. Unknown geometry, missing views and force/noise ambiguities remain.

Actual images and independent simulation checks

Deterministic reference motion is RK4-96. Stochastic references use an independently implemented fine Euler-Maruyama integrator with analytic state-dependent edge amplitudes, coupled Brownian paths at 192/384/768 substeps per frame, audited impulses/supports, and a final-grid consistency tolerance. An evaluation-only oracle-amplitude audit separately checks the production staggered solver at six/twelve substeps. It does not initialize or fit any reconstruction.

Limits and handover

One known 8-node/6-tetrahedron mesh, 30 Gaussians, known cameras/appearance/density/supports, one six-frame schedule and three seeds. Fixed-profile temporal forces, frozen simulator-supervised diffusion, and a retained full-rank floor restrict the conclusions. There is no real-video test, geometry/camera inference, arbitrary force localization, mesh convergence, or proof of calibrated nonlinear uncertainty. The neural network is not identified from the test video, and uncertainty in its calibrated weights is not propagated.

Exact inputs, reference audits/positions, network weights, all fitted solver coordinates, force distributions, per-seed measurements, CSV, plan and source hashes accompany this offline report. Full local precision factors remain in raw checkpoints or are regenerated using the fixed committed plan. Historical reports are preserved.
